terms.meaning: The markup language that gives a web page its structure, such as headings, links and sections.
The styling language that sets colours, fonts, spacing and layout on a web page.
A hidden label in the page header that gives browsers and search engines details such as the page description.
The visible area the page is drawn in, which matters most on phones.
A colour setting with light text on a dark background, which the page can follow from the reader's device.
A hidden link that lets keyboard users jump straight past the header to the main content.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page head, colours and base styles
sections.what: Sets the page description and phone display settings, loads the Archivo typeface, and defines the colour palette for light and dark modes. It also sets base text, link and focus styles, and adds a hidden skip link and a hidden helper for screen readers.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent theming across the page, plus keyboard and screen-reader support. The exact intent of each rule is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The colour values are repeated for light, system dark and forced dark settings, so any colour change must be made in all three places.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Header, buttons and hero styling
sections.what: Sets the look of the sticky top bar with its five coloured blocks and wordmark, the navigation links that hide on narrow screens, the button styles, and the large headline area. It also styles the box that hides a name until it is revealed.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is a styled concept page, so all visual rules sit in one style block without an external design library. Reason for each value not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The blurred header only applies in browsers that support blur, so changing background colours can make the header hard to read in other browsers.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Roster wall and Desk panel styling
sections.what: Lays out the row of five coloured roster tiles with a staggered slide-in animation, and the Desk brief panel with ranked items, sport icons, depth buttons and small trend charts. On phones the roster becomes a horizontally scrolling strip.
sections.why: Likely reason: the stagger makes the tiles appear one after another, and the scroll strip keeps five tiles usable on small screens. Reason not fully stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The stagger depends on a per-tile position value set inline in the HTML, so removing it makes all tiles animate at once.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Make the call panel styling
sections.what: Styles the three moment tabs, the scenario text and fact boxes, the two option buttons with their selected state, and the reveal area with probability bars and grade. It also styles the scorecard that shows the read rating and the list of calls.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reveal compares two options, so bars and grades are styled as visual feedback for each call.
sections.watch_out: The bars grow to their width through script after the page draws, so if the script fails the bars stay empty.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Roster, dossier and footer styling
sections.what: Sets the roster cards with colour bands and labelled details, and the alter ego dossier card that tilts its name once revealed. It also styles the principles grid, the three start steps and the footer.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cards and dossier give the character reveal a finished, trading-card look. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The name tilt applies only when the dossier has the revealed class, so renaming that class silently removes the effect.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Reduced motion and icon set
sections.what: Turns off animations and transitions for visitors whose devices ask for less motion. It also defines a hidden set of five sport pictograms reused wherever an icon appears, plus the skip link and header markup.
sections.why: Likely reason: reduced motion support is an accessibility choice, and one shared icon set avoids repeating drawings.
sections.watch_out: Icons are referenced by their ids, so renaming an icon id leaves an empty space with no error message.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Opening hero and first Desk item
sections.what: Shows the main headline and promise, the buttons, and the hidden alter ego teaser that stays redacted until three calls are made. It also shows the roster tile row, the start of The Desk with its depth switch, and the first ranked brief with its receipt button. The coach-level wording of that first brief is cut off in the material provided, so its exact text is not described here.
sections.why: Likely reason: the opening presents the product promise and examples before the reader reaches the interactive parts.
sections.watch_out: The depth buttons swap text by reading data stored on each brief item, so renaming a depth key breaks that switch.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Remaining Desk briefs and receipts
sections.what: Holds briefs two to five (F1, football, tennis and basketball), each with a headline, depth text, receipt button, mini trend chart and win chance change. In this concept the receipts only describe the source data; they do not open live records. The coach-level text for these briefs is cut off in the material provided, so it is not described here.
sections.why: Likely reason: a concept demo showing how stats would link back to their sources. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: All figures and charts are fixed numbers typed into the page, so they will never change with real results.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Make the call panel layout
sections.what: Lays out the Make the call area: a heading, three moment tabs (cricket, F1, football), a scenario with facts, option buttons, a lock-in button and a reveal area. Beside it is a scorecard showing the read rating, calls made, the ledger and a start over button.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is where the reader makes the three calls that build their alter ego. Reason partly visible in the page wording.
sections.watch_out: The scorecard shows placeholder values (1500 and 0 of 3) until the script fills them in, so those numbers are not live in the markup.

sections.name: File setup (part 10)
sections.title: Roster character cards
sections.what: Describes the five analyst characters, each with a colour, a one-line mentality, a signature tool and a lineage paragraph about a real sports figure. The bench line hints at four future sports.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cards explain each analyst style and tie it to a known athlete. Reason stated only in the page wording.
sections.watch_out: The lineage facts about real people are typed by hand and no code checks them, so an error stays on the page until someone fixes it.

sections.name: File setup (part 11)
sections.title: Alter ego dossier and closing sections
sections.what: Shows the alter ego file card with a hidden name, read rating, calls made, sharpest sport, style and a short reason, plus buttons to make a call and copy the result line. It then gives four principles, three starting steps and a closing button to make the first call.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dossier is the payoff for the three calls, and the closing sections explain the rules. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The copy button stays hidden until the result is shown and its text is set by script, so it copies nothing if the script does not run.

sections.name: File setup (part 12)
sections.title: Footer and interaction helpers
sections.what: Ends the page with footer disclaimers saying this is a working concept with illustrative data. The script then defines short helpers for finding page elements, draws the small trend charts from their listed points, and makes the depth and receipt buttons work.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs simple behaviour for its first interactive parts. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The trend chart drawing divides by the number of points minus one, so a chart with only one point would fail to draw.

sections.name: File setup (part 13)
sections.title: Scenario data and starting state
sections.what: Holds the three moments as data: the cricket over, the F1 pit decision and the football substitution. Each has facts, two options with favoured percentages, a crowd share and written outcomes. It also sets the five character names, the starting rating of 1500 and the shared state of picks and results.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping the content in one list makes scenarios easy to change without touching the logic. Reason stated only as the label toy model.
sections.watch_out: The percentages are fixed numbers from a toy model, not real calculations, so every grade only reflects those chosen figures.

sections.name: File setup (part 14)
sections.title: Selecting an option and drawing a moment
sections.what: The selection step records which option the reader picked, unless that moment is already locked, and updates the button states. The drawing step rebuilds the whole moment panel, including the reveal if that moment was already called.
sections.why: Likely reason: redrawing the full panel keeps the screen in step with the saved state. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Option buttons are rebuilt on every redraw, so any click handler attached to them by hand would disappear.

sections.name: File setup (part 15)
sections.title: Reveal panel and score update
sections.what: The reveal panel shows both options as bars with a favoured marker and the reader's pick, the grade for the call, the simulated outcome and the share of callers who chose the same option. The score update counts the read rating up or down with a short animation and refreshes the calls made count and ledger.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reveal explains the grade so the reader understands why a call scored well or badly.
sections.watch_out: The caller share is calculated as the other option's share for the second option, so it only works for exactly two options.

sections.name: File setup (part 16)
sections.title: Locking in a call and finishing
sections.what: Locking in a call stores the pick, the grade and a random win or loss roll, then changes the rating by twice the grade. When all three moments are called, the finish step picks the alter ego, the sharpest sport and the style, and reveals them on the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the grade shows right away and the alter ego appears only after three calls, as the page promises. Reason for the times-two scoring not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The win or loss roll is random, so the same call can give a different simulated outcome each time, and nothing saves progress if the page reloads.

sections.name: File setup (part 17)
sections.title: Keyboard tabs, reset and copy
sections.what: Lets the reader switch moments by clicking or with the left and right arrow keys, and draws the first moment when the page loads. Start over restores the opening state, and the copy button puts the alter ego line on the clipboard or shows it as text if copying fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: arrow keys follow standard tab behaviour for accessibility, and reset needs copies of the original markup. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Start over restores text from copies taken at page load, so changing the markup of the name or teaser changes what reset brings back.

summary: The opening part of a single-page landing concept, in HTML with built-in styling, meant to introduce ALTER EGO to visitors. Only the page setup and styling are visible here, so the page's body content is not described.
purpose: Defines the look and basic layout for a public landing page for ALTER EGO.
why: Likely reason: a standalone page lets the concept be previewed and shared as a link without running the app.
how: The file starts with the page language, metadata and the Archivo font link. It then defines the colour palette in light and dark versions, sets base typography and layout, and adds hidden helper styles for screen readers and a skip link. The visible part contains no scripts and no page content.
inputs: None in this section. The font loads from Google Fonts when the page opens.
outputs: Styling for the page. On its own, this section shows no visible content, because the page body is in later parts.
risks: Colours are defined for both light and dark settings, so a change can make one version look wrong. The page depends on Google Fonts being reachable.
debug: If the page is unstyled, check the Google Fonts link and that the style block is intact. If dark mode looks wrong, compare the three colour settings near the top of the file.
